title: The leukemia study's depth settled
set_out: The leukemia study first, then the firm rate, then Met-A with the atlas as the ruler, then megakaryocytes and plasma, then replays if machines are free (author's order).

sections.heading: What ran, and how each came out

entries.title: The leukemia study at full depth, complete (GRP-020, DEV-ALL-INFO-01)
entries.what: All 36 samples read at full depth, each against its own molecules.
entries.outcome: All 31 leukemias read above the highest cord-blood control on IAM-A.

entries.title: Liver cancer in blood, replayed (GRP-005, DEV-REPLICATE-01)
entries.what: 481 blood samples, 221 liver cancer cases and 260 controls, read by the one command.
entries.outcome: More neutrophils and monocytes in the cases; Met-A and the territories read the same in both groups.

entries.title: Aging in healthy blood, replayed (DEV-REPLICATE-01)
entries.what: 42 healthy whole bloods aged 18 to 62 read by the one command.
entries.outcome: No instrument reading moves with age across these 42 people.

entries.title: The territories and nearest-neighbor coupling in every document
entries.what: Both added to the instruments document, the book, the glossary, the Introduction and the Decoder, from their sources.
entries.outcome: Every document now carries both, flagged in development.

entries.title: Three chapters loaded into the book
entries.what: The Globe Explorer, the information sphere and Met-A's healthy line, each flagged in development.
entries.outcome: Everything running in the chain is now in the book.

entries.title: Why Met-A reads low on sequencing
entries.what: The atlas's 17 B and T sequencing inputs read against their own columns, with each reading's levels at the identity sites.
entries.outcome: At the unmarked identity sites sequencing reads 0 and the atlas about 0.055, the floor arrays cannot read below; that is the gap.

entries.title: The coupling on the A-score gauge
entries.what: Nearest-neighbor coupling built into the chain as coupling-A, healthy at 1, with a counted floor and ceiling.
entries.outcome: Synthetic met; its healthy reference from the atlas's 153 sequencing inputs is landing.

entries.title: The coupling's healthy reference, built
entries.what: The 153 healthy sequencing samples behind IAM-Atlas v2.1, 56 cell types, read by the one command.
entries.outcome: Healthy coupling differs by cell type (1.30 to 2.18); read against its own cell type a healthy sample sits within 0.935 to 1.062, about a tenth of IAM-A's pooled band. Every sequencing report now draws coupling-A.

entries.title: Met-A on sequencing, read in sequencing units
entries.what: Each atlas column put in sequencing units by the conversion the atlas's own build measured for the published sequencing atlas.
entries.outcome: Planted healthy sequencing samples read 1.00 on average (the array-scale column gave 0.44); its healthy band from the 153 sequencing samples is being read.

entries.title: B and T cells on sequencing: commissioning test written
entries.what: 12 healthy sorted cells from two laboratories the atlas has never held: 4 B cells, 8 CD8 T cells.
entries.outcome: Written before reading: Met-A, coupling-A and IAM-A each must read at least 9 of 12 Normal; queued on the GitHub machines, B cells first.

entries.title: What Normal means on IAM-A
entries.what: IAM-A's commissioned band set beside each healthy cell type's own spread.
entries.outcome: Cell types sit 0.74 to 1.06 while one cell type spans about 0.04: the pooled band's width is mostly between cell types. Every new gauge is built per cell type.

open_at_turnover: Running on GitHub's machines: the firm-rate recount's last sample.
